plain_english_title: Step-by-Step Survivor Checklist After a Veteran Passes Away (Protecting Deadlines, Substitution & Monthly DIC)
what_this_means: In the grief and paperwork following a Veteran's passing, critical VA deadlines can quietly slip by—especially the strict 1-year deadline from the date of death to lock in date-of-death DIC effective dates, open-record Substitution (§ 5121A), and unpaid Accrued Benefits (§ 5121). This step-by-step checklist walks surviving spouses, children, dependent parents, and accredited representatives through the exact records and time-sensitive protections to check: signing a fresh survivor representative appointment, preserving any pending VA or court appeal, checking both service-connected cause of death (§ 1310) and 10-year total-disability DIC (§ 1318), screening for PACT Act or Nehmer Agent Orange retroactivity, and verifying DFAS Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) and burial allowances.
record_clues: The certified death certificate (checking whether contributing service-connected illnesses were omitted), final hospital/hospice discharge summaries, and autopsy reports if performed.
Any VA Rating Decision, Higher-Level Review, Supplemental Claim, Board appeal, or CAVC appeal that was pending—or still within its 1-year / 120-day appeal window—when the Veteran died.
Marriage certificates, prior divorce/death decrees, birth certificates of minor, school-age (18–23), or pre-age-18 permanently disabled ('helpless') children, and funeral/burial receipts.
A Board of Veterans' Appeals decision dated on or after the Veteran's date of death (which must be vacated so the survivor can substitute into the live appeal).
important_cautions: 1-Year Post-Death Deadline Is Strict: Filing VA Form 21P-534EZ and VA Form 21P-0847 within 1 year of death locks in the month-of-death DIC effective date (38 U.S.C. § 5110(d)) AND preserves statutory Substitution and Accrued rights (§§ 5121(c), 5121A). Missing the 1-year mark permanently forfeits non-Nehmer accrued/substitution back pay.
New Representative Form Required: Any VSO or attorney Power of Attorney signed by the Veteran ended at death; the survivor must sign a new VA Form 21-22 or 21-22a.

Dual Filing Required When a Court Appeal Was Pending: If an appeal was at the CAVC or Federal Circuit (or inside the 120-day CAVC appeal window), counsel must protect BOTH court substitution and a formal VA agency substitution/accrued filing within 1 year of death (Merritt v. Wilkie).

Do Not Confuse Post-Mortem CUE With Accrued Pay: A brand-new CUE motion filed for the first time after death cannot pay § 5121 accrued benefits (Haines v. West), though it CAN establish 10-year § 1318 DIC under 38 C.F.R. § 3.22(b)(1).
questions_for_representative: What is the exact 1-year anniversary of the Veteran's passing, and have we submitted both VA Form 21P-534EZ and VA Form 21P-0847 with a fresh survivor VA Form 21-22 / 21-22a?
Did my loved one have any open claim, appeal, unadjudicated issue, or void post-death Board decision into which I can substitute under 38 U.S.C. § 5121A?
Do the final hospital records support contributory service-connected death (§ 3.312(c)), PACT Act DIC re-evaluation (§ 3.33), or 10-year total-disability DIC (§ 3.22)?
Have we also checked non-taxable VA service-connected vs. non-service-connected burial allowances, CHAMPVA health care, Chapter 35 DEA education benefits, and full post-2023 SBP payments?
